title: Flatness at a point ascends under base change and is reflected by a flat base change
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\prime\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Form the fibre product $X\prime=X\times_Y Y\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $a:X\prime\to X$ and $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$. Fix $x\prime\in X\prime$, and put $x=a(x\prime)$ and $y\prime=f\prime(x\prime)$. (1) If $f$ is flat at $x$, then $f\prime$ is flat at $x\prime$. (2) If $g$ is flat at $y\prime$ and $f\prime$ is flat at $x\prime$, then $f$ is flat at $x$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. No finite-type, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 047C, more-morphisms-lemma-flat-locus-base-change, clauses (1) and (2), specialized to the structure sheaf.

proof.text: Put $y=f(x)=g(y\prime)$, $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y\prime,y\prime}$ and $C=\mathcal O_{X\prime,x\prime}$. The equality defining $y$ follows from the projection equation of the fibre product. Use the actual stalk maps to form the commutative square $R\to A$, $R\to B$, $A\to C$, $B\to C$; these are local homomorphisms of local rings by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Set $D=A\otimes_R B$. By [lem-pc-pullback-stalk-tensor-flat], $C$ is flat over $D$ for the map $a\otimes b\mapsto a_Cb_C$, whose restrictions are exactly the projection stalk maps. We use only this stated flatness, not an identification of $C$ with $D$.

source.place: Tag 0FLS, section-silly, paragraph containing can_z; Tag 047C, proof, diagram of local rings

proof.text: For (1), flatness of $f$ at $x$ means that $A$ is flat over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] with base map $R\to B$ and module $A$: $B\otimes_R A$ is flat over $B$. The flip $b\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes b$, with inverse $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$, is a $B$-linear isomorphism onto $D$ with its second-factor $B$-action (the balancing identities show well-definedness and the two composites fix every pure tensor). Thus $D$ is flat over $B$. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] to $B\to D$ and the flat $D$-module $C$ from step 1. It gives that $C$ is flat over $B$, which is exactly flatness of $f\prime$ at $x\prime$.

source.place: Tag 047C, lemma-flat-locus-base-change, proof specialized to the structure sheaf; Algebra Tag 00MQ, lemma-base-change-flat-up-down, (3) and (4)

proof.text: For (2), flatness of $g$ at $y\prime$ gives flatness of $B$ over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] with base map $R\to A$ and module $B$. It gives that $D=A\otimes_R B$ is flat over $A$. Together with step 1, [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] for $A\to D$ and $C$ gives flatness of $C$ over $A$. The composite $A\to D\to C$ is the actual stalk map of the projection $a:X\prime\to X$, so it is a local homomorphism between the local rings $A$ and $C$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] applies and $C$ is faithfully flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 047C, lemma-flat-locus-base-change, proof specialized to the structure sheaf; Algebra Tag 00MQ, lemma-base-change-flat-up-down, (3) and (4)

proof.text: The other hypothesis in (2), flatness of $f\prime$ at $x\prime$, says that $C$ is flat over $B$. Since $B$ is flat over $R$, [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] for $R\to B$ and $C$ makes $C$ flat over $R$. Its $R$-action through $B$ equals the one through $A$ by the commutative stalk square of step 1. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-permanence] to the ring map $R\to A$ and its $A$-module $C$: $C$ is flat over $R$ and faithfully flat over $A$ by step 3, so $A$ is flat over $R$. This is flatness of $f$ at $x$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism], proving (2).
